findings.current:
I thrashed about with all my strength.

I would have struggled with all my strength if I hadn’t realized the truth a moment later.
findings.defect: The English first says the narrator actually thrashed, then says he would have struggled if he had not realized the truth. The Korean corrects itself: he tried to struggle, but did not.
findings.rationale: The source says 몸부림쳤다. 아니, 몸부림치려 했다 (“I struggled. No, I tried to struggle”), then explains he would have done so if he had not realized the situation.
findings.replacement:
I tried to thrash about with all my strength.

I would have, if I hadn’t realized the truth a moment later.

findings.current:
Horses. Monkeys. Leopards. Bears…

Countless among them shone like stars in the night sky before fading away, and eventually, a snow-white White Tiger began guarding the sacred stone.
findings.defect: The English omits the distinction that these creatures had different species and appearances but could hardly be called beasts.
findings.rationale: The source explicitly contrasts their animal forms with their being beyond ordinary beasts; the accepted baseline preserves that distinction.
findings.replacement:
Horses. Monkeys. Leopards. Bears…

Animals of different species and appearances. And yet, they were beings one could hardly call animals.

Countless among them shone like stars in the night sky before fading away, and eventually, a snow-white White Tiger began guarding the sacred stone.

findings.current: Until the moment its blue-white eyes turned black.
findings.defect: The English omits the preceding event: demonic qi seeped into the scars across the guardian spirit’s body.
findings.rationale: The source includes both the qi entering the guardian’s many scars and the later change in its eyes; the accepted baseline preserves both.
findings.replacement: Until demonic qi seeped into the scars covering its body. Until the moment its blue-white eyes turned black.

findings.current:
The moment my fingertips touched it—

*Fwoooooosh!*

At the same time, the column of water walling me in on every side shot into the sky and burst apart like an explosion.
findings.defect: The English omits the dazzling radiance swelling when the narrator touches the object, before the water column shoots up and bursts.
findings.rationale: The source describes the radiance swelling first, then the water column rising and bursting; the sound effect alone does not preserve that visual event.
findings.replacement:
The moment my fingertips touched it—

*Fwoooooosh!*

Dazzling radiance swelled. The column of water walling me in on every side shot into the sky and burst apart like an explosion.

findings.current: No—the new guardian spirit approached and rubbed its head against me.
findings.defect: The English drops “Muyaho,” the name spoken before the narrator corrects himself to “the new guardian spirit.”
findings.rationale: The source explicitly says 무야호. 아니 (“Muyaho. No…”); the glossary also establishes Muyaho as the tiger’s name.
findings.replacement: Muyaho. No—the new guardian spirit approached and rubbed its head against me.

summary: The assembled copy contains several source-detail omissions and one contradiction about whether the narrator actually struggled.
